text.p: The Russian Federal Property Fund (RFFI) has postponed an auction of 1.2 percent of shares in Petersburg Telephone (PTS) originally slated for October 9, a local property official said on Tuesday.
Mikhail Prozorov, in charge of the cash auctions department at the St Petersburg property fund, said he still expected the auction to be held later this year but as a nationwide sale.
"Most probably the RFFI has decided to hold the auction itself, given the large interest in PTS shown by potential investors," Prozorov told Reuters.
RFFI officials said the size and importance of AOOT Sankt-Peterburgskaya Telefonnaya Set meant a local city auction was not appropriate.
"Companies like PTS should be sold at an all-Russian or at least inter-regional auction," Vladimir Yefimchik, head of the RFFI's information and analysis department, told Reuters.
Yefimchik did not name a new date for the auction, but said St Petersburg property officials had been ordered to prepare the necessary regulations for a broader auction.
"The date will be set once they have completed all the preparations for the auction," he said.
The St Petersburg property fund was offering 186,594 shares with a nominal value of 50 roubles at a starting price of 50,000 roubles per share.
State holding telecommunications company AO Svyazinvest is the biggest shareholder of Petersburg Telephone, and controls 41.8 percent of its shares.
Bank St Petersburg said in August it had sold a 12 percent share in Petersburg Telephone, but refused to name the buyer.
The authorised capital of Petersburg Telephone is 777.46 billion roubles.
